clue.text: Corrupt old rebel be set by depression

indicators.note: to be set by something is to be placed within it, so the rebel goes inside the depression

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A rebel from history is denounced as rotten, his base sunk in a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes morally degenerate, self-indulgent behaviour, much as corrupt does.

clue.text: Curse dunderheaded renegade

parts.note: read as dunder-headed: the head of the word dunder is its letter D, placed at the top of this down entry
a rat is someone who deserts their side

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a stupid turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderheaded' plays on its parts: something headed by the first letter of dunder, so D comes before RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation of annoyance, used like a curse.

clue.text: A scene prepared for spiritualists

indicators.note: the letters of a scene are prepared, made ready in a new order

explanation.surface: A setting is arranged for a group of mediums.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting at which spiritualists try to contact the dead, arranged as a scene for them.

clue.text: Emerge without warning in gun fight

explanation.surface: Someone appears suddenly in the middle of a gun battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring out suddenly is to shoot out; a decisive exchange of gunfire is a shoot-out.

clue.text: Restless excitement one month before G & S opera

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Patience is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: Someone is eager and fidgety in the month leading up to a Gilbert and Sullivan show.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is restless eagerness, an inability to wait calmly.

clue.text: Senior cleric takes care of minor one

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the senior cleric swallows the abbreviation

parts.note: a dean heads a cathedral chapter
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A high-ranking churchman looks after a junior colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained cleric of the lowest rank, a minor one beside a dean.

clue.text: Best not to look so much?

explanation.surface: The advice is that it is better not to stare too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without equal, unmatched; and to peer less is to gaze less intently.

clue.text: The gullible guy is a dummy

explanation.surface: The easily fooled man is called a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker is a dupe easily taken in; it is also a teat or pacifier, a baby's dummy.

clue.text: Radio buff rented small place in the country

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast
a let property is one rented out

explanation.surface: An amateur radio enthusiast rents a cottage out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a tiny rural settlement, smaller than a village.

clue.text: Not slow to refrain from eating

explanation.surface: Someone is quick to skip meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast means quick; to fast is to go without food.

clue.text: Terrible concern may result from witchcraft

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of concern may are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Dreadful worry may come of dabbling in the occult.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromancy is sorcery, especially conjuring the dead, a form of black magic.

clue.text: A place to meet round Inns of Court

indicators.note: round signals that the letters are turned around into a fresh order

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Lawyers gather at a meeting spot near the London law colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inner and Middle Temple are two of London's four Inns of Court, the societies that call barristers to the bar; 'round' as an anagram signal means turned about.
explanation.definitionFit: The Temple is the London district housing two of the four barristers' societies.

clue.text: Wealthy magician going to America

indicators.note: going to places the second piece after the first

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A conjuror travels to the United States and gets rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means flourishing financially, well off.

clue.text: Item soon generated strong feelings

indicators.note: generated signals that the letters of item soon produce a new word

explanation.surface: A news story soon stirred people up.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotions are feelings such as love, anger or fear.

clue.text: Nevertheless, meditated endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: to have meditated is to have thought

explanation.surface: Even so, someone pondered without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Though can mean however or all the same, as in 'he came, though'.

clue.text: Mailed glove to Duke of Lancaster — that's permitted

parts.note: John of Gaunt was Duke of Lancaster, son of Edward III
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A knight's armoured glove is given to a medieval duke, by permission.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is an armoured glove worn with a suit of chain mail.

clue.text: School includes small number in bad odour

indicators.note: includes means the school abbreviation holds the number inside

parts.note: ten is a smallish number

explanation.surface: A school is in trouble over a handful of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bad odour' sounds like disgrace, but 'bad odour' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a foul smell.

clue.text: Intractable man, difficult to put on trial

parts.note: hard means difficult
a case is a matter tried in court

explanation.surface: A stubborn fellow is tricky to bring before a court.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard case is a tough, unruly person who will not be reformed.

clue.text: He sees edition as drawback

parts.note: read as draw back: the word draw written backwards gives these letters

explanation.surface: A man regards a published version as a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like a disadvantage but splits as draw + back: DRAW reversed gives WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is a man's name, so 'he' is an example.

clue.text: Make submission against the euro?

explanation.surface: Someone lodges an objection to the single currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to put forward for consideration; being pro-pound means favouring sterling over the euro.

clue.text: Go and change partners

explanation.surface: Dancers are told to move on and swap partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is to go there; to re-pair is to match up again.

clue.text: Not clear how barley is processed

indicators.note: processing changes something, so the letters of barley are reworked

explanation.surface: It is unclear how grain is handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are blurred and dim, not clear-sighted.

clue.text: How one may gain access to ring road?

explanation.surface: Directions explain the way onto an orbital route.
explanation.definitionFit: By pass means by showing a permit; a bypass is a road skirting a town.

clue.text: What Aladdin used to summon the genie?

definitions.text: What Aladdin used to summon the genie?

parts.words: What Aladdin used to summon the genie?
parts.note: Aladdin rubbed a lamp to call up its spirit, so the lamp is read as a lamp for a spirit, though really it is one burning alcohol

explanation.surface: A question about the magic lamp in the Arabian Nights story.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp fuelled by methylated spirit, punningly the lamp that held a spirit.

clue.text: Speed of movement recorded in account of exercise

indicators.note: recorded in means written inside, so the account goes into the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A record is kept of how fast someone moves during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace is rate of progress, as of walking or running.

clue.text: Perhaps it's needed when Penny gets sick

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Medicine may be called for when a girl named Penny falls unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet of medicine is something one needs when sick.

clue.text: Very small log

explanation.surface: A tiny piece of firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute means tiny; to minute is to record in writing.

clue.text: Reveal the daughter is at hand

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
close means near, at hand

explanation.surface: Someone discloses that their daughter is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known, to uncover.
